title: Ranked task-name matches
description: Umbra task/site names ranked by how well they match a plain-language query, emitted by `umbra semantic search --json`. The semantic answer to a site you can describe but cannot name: the query is embedded and scored against the stored task-name embeddings, and what comes back is a list of names that *exist in the catalog* — a model contributes the ranking, never the name. Empty `matches` means nothing cleared the score threshold, which is an answer rather than a failure.

query.description: The plain-language query, echoed so a stored result says what it was searching for.
examples: a copper mine in the desert

matches.description: The candidates that cleared the threshold, closest first. `matches[0].task` is what `umbra search --area` would be run with.

task.description: The Umbra task/site name, verbatim from the catalog — the argument `umbra search --area` takes.

score.description: Cosine similarity to the query, rounded to six places: 1.0 identical, 0.0 unrelated, higher is closer. A measurement a test can recompute, not a model's opinion of its own answer.
